summary: Describes a Transport Security Model for SNMP, which lets SNMP take its security identity from a secure underlying transport. It also defines part of the MIB for monitoring and managing that model.

plainLanguage.summary: The SNMP Transport Security Model lets SNMP rely on security provided by an underlying transport, such as a secure shell transport. It carries the transport's identity into SNMP, but the transport itself must provide the protection.

subtitle: Let SNMP use identity and protection supplied by a secure transport.

tldr.problem: SNMP needs a way to use secure lower-layer transports without tying its security model to one transport or its cryptographic details.
tldr.mechanism: The Transport Security Model maps the secure transport's identity and security level into SNMP security parameters, and defines MIB counters and a prefix setting.
tldr.outcome: TSM provides no authentication or encryption itself; it relies on an appropriately configured secure Transport Model.

today: RFC 5591 is an Internet Standard. It defines the SNMP Transport Security Model and its management information base.

sections.title: Using Security from the Transport
sections.content:
The Transport Security Model (TSM) is designed for secure Transport Models in the SNMP Transport Subsystem. It lets SNMP use a secure transport and its existing security infrastructure while keeping the SNMP architecture modular.

TSM defines both processing procedures and part of a Management Information Base (MIB) for monitoring and configuring the model.
sections.plainLanguage: TSM connects SNMP to a secure transport instead of defining a separate transport-security protocol. It also provides management data for the model.

sections.title: How TSM Fits into SNMP
sections.content:
For an incoming message, a secure Transport Model supplies a cached transport-state reference with a transport identity and asserted security level. TSM turns that identity into an SNMP security name and checks that the transport's security level is at least the level requested by the SNMP message-processing model.

For outgoing messages, TSM creates or reuses the transport-state reference and passes it to the selected Transport Model. TSM trusts the Transport Model's report about its security services.
sections.plainLanguage: The transport reports who connected and what security it used. TSM passes that identity into SNMP and checks that the reported protection is sufficient.

sections.title: Processing Incoming Messages
sections.content:
TSM requires a valid transport-state cache containing the transport domain, address, security name, and security level. It copies the transport security name into the SNMP security name, optionally adding a prefix associated with the transport domain.

If the transport did not provide the authentication or privacy level requested by the message, TSM returns an error and increments the inadequate-security-level counter. It retains the transport state so a response can use the same security parameters.
sections.plainLanguage: For an incoming message, TSM checks that transport information is present and that the connection used enough security. If a response is needed, it can reuse the same connection identity and settings.

sections.title: Configuration and Monitoring
sections.content:
The SNMP-TSM-MIB defines error counters for invalid caches, inadequate security levels, unknown prefixes, and invalid prefixes. Its configuration object controls whether a transport-domain prefix is added to security names.

The prefix option is false by default. The counters help an administrator identify configuration or processing failures in the Transport Security Model.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIB lets administrators see why TSM rejected messages and choose whether transport names include a domain prefix. The prefix setting starts disabled.

sections.title: Security Comes from the Transport
sections.content:
TSM does not authenticate peers, bind keys, encrypt messages, or check integrity itself. Those services and the threats they address depend on the Transport Model and its underlying secure transport.

Operators must pair TSM with a Transport Model that provides appropriate security. Access to the MIB configuration object also needs protection because changing it can affect authorization decisions.
sections.plainLanguage: TSM does not make an insecure connection secure. The chosen Transport Model must provide the authentication, privacy, and integrity that the deployment requires.
